report.source_text: After eight days, he demonstrated good response to treatment; Glasgow Coma Scale improved to 15, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia improved, and mRS score reduced to 2. He was discharged home after 16 days with residual deficits including mild ophthalmoplegia, upper limb dysmetria with intention tremor, mild aphasia, and dysarthria. At discharge, mRS score was 1. Two weeks later, mRS score improved to 0, indicating neurological function recovery.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 11-year-old boy presented with acute febrile illness and SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed by acute neurological deterioration including ophthalmoplegia and cerebellar signs. Brain MRI demonstrated characteristic bilateral thalamic, brainstem, cerebellar, and periventricular white matter lesions with diffusion restriction and blood products consistent with ANEC. CSF analysis showed elevated protein, no pleocytosis, negative infectious panel including SARS-CoV-2 PCR, and negative autoimmune markers in serum and CSF. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and his ANEC severity score indicated high risk for poor outcome. Treatment with IV methylprednisolone and IVIG was initiated. Clinical course showed significant neurological improvement by eight days and near complete recovery by two weeks post-discharge.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Brain MRI showed swelling and signal changes involving bilateral thalami, midbrain, pons, cerebellar hemispheres, and periventricular white matter consistent with ANEC.
CSF analysis revealed elevated protein without pleocytosis, normal glucose and lactate, negative infectious and SARS-CoV-2 PCR panel, and absent oligoclonal bands.
Extensive serum and CSF autoimmune tests were negative, excluding autoimmune encephalitis.
Elevated systemic inflammatory markers including ESR, CRP, and procalcitonin supported inflammatory state.
High ANEC severity score (5 of 9) indicated risk for neurological poor outcome.
Treatment with IV methylprednisolone 1000 mg daily for 5 days and IVIG 2 g/kg administered promptly.
Clinical improvement observed by 8 days post-treatment with improved neurological signs and near full recovery at 2 weeks post-discharge.
Imaging further demonstrated CT hypodensity and MRI findings of diffusion restriction and hemorrhage consistent with ANEC.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: CSF negative for infectious pathogens including SARS-CoV-2 PCR; no pleocytosis
Extensive negative autoimmune antibody panels in serum and CSF
